topic: What spectral efficiency challenges arise from real-time adaptation to sparsely distributed channels in Inmarsat's BGAN signals?
response: Inmarsat's BGAN signals exhibit spectral efficiency challenges due to real-time adaptation to sparsely distributed channels. The use of 16 QAM and 0.25 root raised cosine filters in each 200 kHz channel may lead to increased noise susceptibility, compromising the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Additionally, the high symbol rate of 151.2 ksymbol/s might exacerbate these issues.
reference_context: Inmarsat BGAN signals use 16 QAM and 0.25 root raised cosine filters in each 200 kHz channel with a symbol rate of 151.2 ksymbol/s. The signal is transmitted using FDD TDMA modulation, and the system has 630 channels with frequency reuse or 170 frequency channels.
